name: Ivacaftor
route_note: Oral tablets or granules twice daily with fat-containing food; also a component of combination CFTR modulators
originator: Vertex Pharmaceuticals (with Cystic Fibrosis Foundation funding)

discovery.by: Vertex Pharmaceuticals (high-throughput screening programme begun at Aurora Biosciences)
discovery.note: Identified by cell-based screening for compounds that increase CFTR channel opening.

tagline: First drug to treat the underlying defect in cystic fibrosis
summary: Ivacaftor is a CFTR potentiator that increases the open probability of defective chloride channels at the cell surface. Approved in 2012 for patients with the G551D gating mutation, it was the first therapy to target the cause of cystic fibrosis and is a backbone of later combination modulators.
mechanism: Gating mutations such as G551D produce CFTR protein that reaches the cell membrane but rarely opens. Ivacaftor binds CFTR and stabilises its open state, increasing chloride transport independently of ATP-driven gating.
Restored ion transport lowers sweat chloride, improves airway surface liquid and mucociliary clearance, and improves lung function and weight.
uses: Cystic fibrosis in patients with at least one gating or other ivacaftor-responsive CFTR mutation (from 1 month of age)
Component of lumacaftor/ivacaftor, tezacaftor/ivacaftor and elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor

history.title: STRIVE trial
history.detail: Phase 3 trial in G551D patients shows ~10-point ppFEV1 improvement and large falls in sweat chloride.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Kalydeco in January for patients aged 6 and older with G551D.

history.title: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor
history.detail: FDA approves Orkambi for F508del homozygous patients.

history.title: Mutation expansion
history.detail: FDA expands the label using in vitro response data, an unusual regulatory approach.

history.title: Infants
history.detail: FDA extends Kalydeco to infants aged 1 month and older.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A to active M1 and inactive M6 metabolites

serious: Interactions with strong CYP3A inducers and inhibitors

facts: Ivacaftor's development was partly funded by the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation, which later sold its royalty rights for $3.3 billion.
Ivacaftor is also the potentiator in Vertex's combination products.
